description: Multiple shifts must keep medication timing, feeding notes, stool observations, and behavior changes consistent for animals under treatment without dropping critical context at shift change.

fact_sheet.fact: Baxter is a 4-year-old male neutered Beagle mix, animal ID A4512, weighing 28 lbs (12.7 kg).
Baxter is housed in the Medical Recovery wing, Kennel M-03, due to a recent diagnosis of pancreatitis.
Luna is a 2-year-old female spayed Domestic Shorthair, animal ID C8901, weighing 9 lbs (4.1 kg).
Luna is housed in Medical Isolation, Kennel I-05, for treatment of an Upper Respiratory Infection (URI).
Baxter receives 20mg of Famotidine orally every 12 hours; doses are scheduled for 08:00 and 20:00.
Baxter is prescribed 75mg of Gabapentin orally every 8 hours for pain management, with doses at 06:00, 14:00, and 22:00.
Luna receives 20mg of Doxycycline liquid suspension (5mg/ml concentration) orally once daily at 09:00.
All medications administered must be initialed on the paper kennel card and digitally logged in ShelterCare Pro within 5 minutes.
Baxter is on a strict diet of 1/2 cup of Hill's Prescription Diet i/d Low Fat kibble, fed twice daily at 08:30 and 20:30.
Baxter's water intake is monitored; his bowl is refilled to the 500ml line at the start of each shift (07:00, 15:00, 23:00).
Luna is offered 1/4 can of Royal Canin Recovery wet food mixed with 15ml of warm water three times daily at 07:30, 15:30, and 23:30 to encourage eating.
The percentage of food consumed by Luna at each meal must be estimated and logged (e.g., 'ate 50%').
All stool from Baxter must be scored using the on-wall Bristol Stool Chart (1-7 scale) and the score logged in his digital file under 'GI Observation'.
Any instance of vomiting from Baxter, including volume and consistency, must be immediately reported to the on-call veterinarian, Dr. Evan Reed.
Luna's respiratory rate must be counted over 60 seconds while she is resting; this must be done and logged once per shift.
The type of Luna's nasal discharge (clear, yellow, green) and presence of sneezing must be noted in the 'URI Progress' section of her log at least twice per shift.
Baxter has shown food guarding behavior; staff must place his food bowl down and step away from the kennel door immediately after.
A 'low-stress handling' flag is active for Luna; she responds best to slow movements and minimal direct eye contact.
On October 25th at 21:15, Baxter exhibited lethargy and refused his evening walk, a change from his previously energetic behavior.
Shift change occurs daily at 07:00, 15:00, and 23:00.
A mandatory 15-minute verbal and digital handover between the outgoing and incoming vet tech must occur at the central medical workstation (Desk M1).
The outgoing technician must update the 'Shift Summary' field in ShelterCare Pro for all animals in the Medical wing before clocking out.
Anya Sharma is the Lead Veterinary Technician and is responsible for overseeing medical treatment plans.
Dr. Evan Reed is the primary veterinarian on call for medical emergencies; his pager number is 555-010-9876.
Carlos Diaz is the overnight veterinary technician, working the 23:00 to 07:00 shift.
The ShelterCare Pro system is accessed via the URL: https://pawsanctuary.sheltercarepro.com/login.
All vet techs use a shared login for the medical workstation PC: username 'medtech' with password 'Care4Paws2023!'.
Urgent, non-emergency updates for the next shift are posted in the '#med-team-handoff' Slack channel.
The secure medication lockbox is located in the primary treatment room, cabinet C. The access code is 10-26-08.
The isolation ward (I-wing) requires full PPE (gown, gloves, shoe covers) before entry; the PPE station is located just outside the main door.
In case of a Code Blue (animal medical emergency), press the red button located next to the phone at the central medical station.
The emergency veterinary hospital is Northwood Animal Hospital, located at 123 Veterinary Lane, phone 555-012-3456.
